name: Gujarati
signature: Looks like Devanagari with the head-line erased — round tops and no bar running across the top.
combination: A consonant carries an inherent 'a' (ક = ka). A vowel mark (mātrā) replaces that vowel (ક + ી → કી = kī). The virama ્ strips the vowel, and the bare consonant joins the next into a conjunct (ન + ્ + મ → ન્મ). Gujarati is Devanagari's sister, but with one visible difference: it has NO horizontal top line (shirorekhā) — the letters float free, which is why it is sometimes called 'the headless script.'
notes: Used by Gujarati (the language of Gandhi). The initial inventory below covers the greeting/self-introduction/first-verbs vocabulary; it grows toward a complete set. Letterforms mirror Devanagari without the top bar. Stroke orders are the common handwriting convention, not a standard.

components: a joined left curve and lower body
a middle shoulder and small right arch
a separate right stem with a foot
strokeOrder: begin at the upper-left tip and sweep clockwise around the open left curve
continue through the lower body and rise into the middle shoulder
retrace down the shoulder and sweep through the small right arch to its junction
lift once, descend the separate right stem, and curve into its lower-right foot
letters.strokeOrderNote: verified two-stroke teaching-app variant fitted to the bundled printed outline

strokeOrderSource.citation: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, અ animation, first and second SVG paths
strokeOrderSource.variation: The teaching app animates અ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper-left tip, sweeps clockwise around the open left curve, continues through the broad lower body, rises into the middle shoulder, and finishes through the small right arch. The animation then lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate right stem before curving into the lower-right foot. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph has the same open left curve, joined lower body, middle shoulder, small right arch, and separate full-height right stem, but its printed proportions are broader and its joins more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's body-before-right-stem order and one-lift evidence while fitting those movements to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, or slant either run differently.
